response.sql: SELECT i.invoice_number, AVG(li.derived_total_cost * 1.0 / NULLIF(li.derived_product_cost, 0)) AS avg_cost_ratio, COUNT(li.order_item_id) AS line_item_count FROM Invoices i LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items li ON li.invoice_number = i.invoice_number GROUP BY i.invoice_number ORDER BY line_item_count DESC, i.invoice_number ASC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The average is the mean of each line item's own ratio (derived_total_cost / derived_product_cost), not the ratio of the summed totals. Line items with a NULL or zero derived_product_cost produce a NULL ratio and are skipped by AVG. The schema does not say whether those values can occur.

Invoices with no line items get a count of 0 and a NULL average, via the LEFT JOIN and COUNT of the line item key. Invoices are ranked by line item count descending, with ties broken by invoice_number ascending. The request does not settle tie order at the 10th position.

alternatives.interpretation: The ratio is computed from the invoice's totals: sum of derived_total_cost divided by sum of derived_product_cost across its line items, giving one aggregate ratio per invoice rather than an average of per-line ratios.
alternatives.sql: SELECT i.invoice_number, SUM(li.derived_total_cost) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(li.derived_product_cost), 0) AS cost_ratio, COUNT(li.order_item_id) AS line_item_count FROM Invoices i LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items li ON li.invoice_number = i.invoice_number GROUP BY i.invoice_number ORDER BY line_item_count DESC, i.invoice_number ASC LIMIT 10;
